theory.title: Shops, clothes, prices and paying
theory.explanation: Use this and that with singular nouns, and these and those with plural nouns. Ask How much is this ...? for one item and How much are these ...? for more than one. Use comparatives such as cheaper than and more expensive than to compare prices. Use too + adjective when something is more than you want, and adjective + enough when something is sufficient. Ask politely to try something on, check a size or pay by card.
theory.tip: This jacket is singular, these shoes are plural. Say try it on or try them on, and remember that trousers and jeans are plural.

content.passage: Ella is looking for a jacket for winter. In the first shop, she sees a black jacket for £60. It is nice, but it is too expensive. In another shop, she finds a blue jacket for £45. She asks the shop assistant, “Have you got this in a small size?” The assistant brings one, and Ella tries it on. It fits well, but the sleeves are a little long. She also tries a green jacket, which is cheaper, but it isn't warm enough. Ella prefers the blue jacket. She pays by card and keeps the receipt.

content.audioTranscript: Good afternoon. Can I help you? Yes, I'm looking for a pair of trainers. What size are you? I'm a size seven. We have these in black and white. How much are the black ones? They're forty pounds. And the white ones? They're thirty-five pounds, so they're cheaper. Can I try them on? Of course. The fitting rooms are over there. The white ones are comfortable. I'll take them. Can I pay by card? Certainly. Here's your receipt. We also have a medium size in the shop.
